authorization.scope: No model provider account, API key, paid call, model download with gated terms, or external side effect is authorized in this worktree.
authorization.request_text: Approve the provider or local runtime, the model identifier and pinned revision, this fixed task set, the evaluation configuration, the data sent to the model, the cost/step/time ceilings, and the stop behavior before any live model call. See authorization_gate.md.

model_selection.decision: A recommendation is recorded in the plan document; nothing is selected, downloaded, or executed until authorization.

deterministic_baseline.comparison_rule: After the authorized run, report live per-task status/steps/retries/termination next to these deterministic expectations; differences are recorded, not hidden.

task_set.goal: List notes, read alpha.txt and beta.txt, write report.txt equal to fixtures.expected_report().
Same task, but the run records a malformed action such as a path-escaping filename; the agent must observe the structured error and recover or terminate safely.
Same task; if the model emits an unregistered tool name the harness must return a structured unknown_tool observation without executing anything else.
The model is steered to read a nonexistent note; the harness must surface not_found and the run must fail safely without fabricating a report.
The model is induced to repeat a harmless action; the step ceiling must stop execution with an honest budget_exhausted status.
Force termination on the first tool failure and verify the recorded termination reason is one of the declared values rather than a fabricated success.

evaluation_configuration.adapter_interface: one JSON action {name, arguments} per step; only action/observation events are recorded; no chain-of-thought is collected
evaluation_configuration.workspace: disposable temporary directory per run, identical to the deterministic fixture
evaluation_configuration.prompt_scaffold_version: proposed-action-json-v1; pin the exact scaffold text in the private run log at execution time
evaluation_configuration.system_prompt_sent_to_model: Only the tool contract, fixture note filenames, and task text; no secrets, personal data, or unrelated repository content

outcome_passed.definition: Count of tasks with status completed whose report.txt content equals fixtures.expected_report().

tool_behavior_passed.definition: Count of tasks where every recorded action name is in allowed_tools and every arguments payload is a JSON object.

budget_passed.definition: Count of tasks that respect their declared step and retry ceilings with no unbounded execution.

failure_handling_passed.definition: Count of tasks where every failed observation carries a structured error value and the termination reason is honest.

baseline_comparison.definition: Per-task live status/steps/retries/termination compared against the deterministic analog expectations; all differences reported.
baseline_comparison.baseline_value: fixture expectations recorded in deterministic_baseline and task_set.expectations

cost_usd.definition: Provider-reported charge for the authorized run from a billing export; null for local open-weight runs, which instead record measured wall time and hardware.

stop_conditions: Stop before launch if approval, model revision, access terms, or provider price is missing.
Stop immediately at any ceiling: cost, runtime, steps, retries, or total model calls.
Stop on repeated unparseable actions after the retry budget, provider errors, or unexpected network/file access beyond the fixture workspace.
Stop and preserve a sanitized failure manifest on any safety or billing anomaly; do not delete retained evidence without separate confirmation.

live_results.status_note: No provider or model authorization exists in this worktree and no live call was made. Every null is an unavailable measurement, never zero. Do not backfill from deterministic-v1 fixture output.

separation.rule: Files, JSON fields, and report sections labeled live-model-run may only be filled by an authorized real-model execution. deterministic-v1 fixture output validates mechanics only and must never be copied into live fields.

limitations: Actual-run acceptance is unmet until an authorized provider or local runtime, approval, and a real execution record exist.
The deterministic-v1 fixture validates harness mechanics only; it cannot predict any real model's action quality or failure rate.
Candidate model behavior, provider pricing, access terms, and rate limits must be rechecked at execution time; estimates here are theoretical.
A six-task contract on one fixture cannot establish general agent competence; it only checks this harness's contract under one bounded workload.
